wa.gloss: marks the topic — what the sentence is about

ga.gloss: marks the subject, and the object of 〜たい

o.gloss: marks the direct object — the thing acted on

ni.gloss: marks a destination, a point in time, or where something is

de.gloss: marks the means, or where an action happens

mo.gloss: replaces は or が to mean "too" or "also"

no.gloss: joins two nouns — possession, or one describing the other

e.gloss: marks the direction of movement — softer than に

to.gloss: joins nouns as a complete list, or marks who with

ka.gloss: turns a sentence into a question

made.gloss: marks the end point — "as far as", "until"

masu.name: polite non-past
masu.note: Attach ます to the verb stem: 止まり + ます. This is the form to default to with anyone you are not close to.

mashita.name: polite past
mashita.note: The past of ます is ました, on the same stem: 止まり + ました. です does not take it — it becomes でした.

masen.name: polite negative
masen.note: The negative of ます is ません, on the same stem: 止まり + ません. Nothing else in the sentence changes.

te-form.name: te-form
te-form.note: The connective form — it joins clauses and carries ている, てください and much else. Ichidan verbs take て on the stem; godan verbs change the ending by its final sound.

tai.name: want to
tai.note: Attach たい to the verb stem: 食べ + たい. It behaves as an adjective afterwards, and its object takes が rather than を.

potential.name: potential
potential.note: "Can do" — 払え, 使え. What the verb could act on becomes が rather than を, because the potential describes a state rather than an action.
